CockroachDB

Source: vignettes/cockroachdb.Rmd
cockroachdb.Rmd

Use oauth_db_cockroachdb() to query a self-hosted or cloud CockroachDB cluster with each Shiny visitor’s account and database permissions. The helper opens an RPostgres connection that works with DBI and dbplyr.

The cluster must accept JWT access tokens from your identity provider. Signing in to the CockroachDB Cloud console alone doesn’t establish SQL access. This guide uses cluster SSO with JWTs, where the client supplies the access token as its SQL password over verified TLS.

Before running the app

Install RPostgres linked to libpq 16 or later. To check the version, run DBI::dbGetInfo(RPostgres::Postgres())$client.version. On Linux, install the corresponding libpq development package before building RPostgres. This backend works on Windows, macOS and Linux; it doesn’t need the Linux-only native PostgreSQL OAuth hook in shinyOAuthDB.

Your administrator must enable JWT SQL authentication and configure the trusted issuer, signing keys, audience and username mapping. Register a Shiny OAuth client with that provider using the authorization code flow. It must issue JWT-format access tokens with the configured audience and principal claim. This helper doesn’t substitute an ID token when the provider issues opaque access tokens.

Save these settings in .Renviron and restart R:

Setting Where to get it
OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_HOST The cluster’s SQL connection hostname
OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_DATABASE A database the visitor can query
OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_ISSUER The cluster’s trusted OIDC issuer
OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_AUDIENCE The audience configured for the cluster’s access tokens
OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_SSLROOTCERT CA bundle for the SQL endpoint, or empty to use libpq’s configured bundle
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID, OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET Your provider’s app registration

The example requests database.read, an example scope your provider must define or replace. It uses the validated login’s preferred_username claim as the requested SQL username. Configure the access token and CockroachDB to map to that same username, or change the user function to match your organization’s mapping. The database verifies that the token may use the requested SQL user.

A complete app

The app lists tables visible to the signed-in user. Register http://localhost:8100 as the redirect URI.

After signing in, click Load rows. The app starts its workers once and stops them at shutdown.

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

audience <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_AUDIENCE")

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_ISSUER"),
  extra_auth_params = if (nzchar(audience)) {
    list(audience = audience)
  } else {
    list()
  }
)

client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "database.read")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),

    actionButton("load", "Load rows"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),

  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )

  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  ca <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_SSLROOTCERT")

  con <- oauth_db_cockroachdb(
    auth$connection,
    host = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_HOST"),
    dbname = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_COCKROACHDB_DATABASE"),
    user = function() {
      reference <- req(auth$connection())
      identity <- reference$identity(claims = "preferred_username")
      req(identity$id_token_claims$preferred_username)
    },
    sslrootcert = if (nzchar(ca)) {
      ca
    } else {
      NULL
    },
    required_scopes = "database.read"
  )

  query_task <- oauth_db_task(con)

  observeEvent(input$load, {
    query_task$invoke(paste(
      "SELECT table_schema, table_name FROM information_schema.tables",
      "WHERE table_schema NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema', 'crdb_internal')",
      "ORDER BY table_schema, table_name LIMIT 20"
    ))
  })

  output$rows <- renderTable(query_task$result())
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)

    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at its registered redirect URI.

Some providers configure the audience in the app registration or with a resource parameter rather than an audience authorization parameter. Adjust the provider configuration to match your identity service. See Getting started for shared registration settings and deployment.

Configure the cluster

Follow CockroachDB’s cluster SSO guide for the settings supported by your cluster version and cloud tier. A configuration using a trusted OIDC provider includes:

SET CLUSTER SETTING server.jwt_authentication.enabled = true;
SET CLUSTER SETTING server.jwt_authentication.issuers.configuration =
  'https://login.example.org/realms/reporting';
SET CLUSTER SETTING server.jwt_authentication.audience = 'shiny-reporting';
SET CLUSTER SETTING server.jwt_authentication.claim = 'preferred_username';
SET CLUSTER SETTING server.jwt_authentication.jwks_auto_fetch.enabled = true;

Create the corresponding SQL users and grant their database permissions, or configure the cluster’s supported provisioning and role-mapping features. A JWT login doesn’t grant access to every table. You can also configure static JWKS keys, but your administrator must keep them current as the identity provider rotates signing keys.

The helper sets options = "--crdb:jwt_auth_enabled=true", supplies the access token as the password and requires password authentication from the server. It uses sslmode = "verify-full" to verify the certificate and hostname. Supply the CA bundle from the cluster’s connection settings when libpq’s configured bundle doesn’t include it. Unset PGSERVICE and PGSERVICEFILE so local service files cannot change the connection.

CockroachDB also supports SASL OAUTHBEARER on newer clusters with libpq 18 clients. This helper uses JWT-as-password authentication instead, so it requires the server.jwt_authentication configuration rather than the separate server.oauthbearer_authentication configuration.

Connections and token renewal

Create the helper inside server() and get connection <- con() before each operation. The accessor reuses its connection until the token or SQL username changes, the connection becomes invalid, or the authorization ends. After token renewal, the next call replaces the connection; renewal alone doesn’t rerun a completed reactive query.

Account changes, lost required permissions, sign-out and session end close the connection. Keep each transaction on the connection that started it, and use con() again for the next operation. A native connection retained elsewhere can still hold copied credentials; use the accessor for subsequent operations.
